name: work-timing-policy
purpose: Defines how workspace tasks record phase timings so bottlenecks are visible in history, evaluations, coordination boards, and monitoring views.

reader_guide.summary: Use this file before and after meaningful work to decide which timing phases to record and how to interpret bottlenecks. Timing is an observability aid, not a productivity score.
how_to_read: Read structure_rules before changing the timing schema.
Use standard_phases as the default phase vocabulary for new timing records.
Use bottleneck_thresholds to understand when a phase should be called out.
Use field_guide when creating or reviewing a _history/work-timings record.
Run _tools/work-timer/src/work_timer.py check after creating or editing a timing record.
update_triggers: The user changes how work time or bottlenecks should be recorded.
Work modes or evaluator target policy changes.
Coordination board or Workspace Monitor needs a different timing display.
A new repeated phase appears across many tasks.
The timing tool starts producing misleading bottleneck summaries.

structure_rules.rule: Record task time as named phase spans, not only as a total duration.
structure_rules.reason: A total time value does not reveal where the bottleneck occurred.

structure_rules.rule: If a phase was not measured from the start, mark measurement_quality as partial or phase measurement as not_measured instead of inventing exact times.
structure_rules.reason: Timing data should help decisions without creating false precision.

structure_rules.rule: Treat the slowest measured phase as a bottleneck candidate and record bottleneck_notes before using it to change the workflow.
structure_rules.reason: Long duration can reflect necessary work, external waiting, or missing tooling; the note prevents shallow optimization.

structure_rules.rule: Meaningful standard, research, and governance work should include timing_summary_targets in evaluator input.
structure_rules.reason: The user asked to make bottlenecks easy to see for each task.

structure_rules.rule: Coordination tasks should link their timing_report when a timing record exists.
structure_rules.reason: Active and recent work should show elapsed time and bottleneck candidates in one place.

field_guide.meaning: Stable task identifier, normally matching the request trace or coordination task id.
Selected work mode for the task.
Overall timing quality: measured, partial, or not_measured.
List of timing spans. Each phase should include phase_id, label, status, and either duration_seconds or started_at plus ended_at when measured.
Human-readable interpretation of the slowest phase, external waits, and improvement candidates.
Optional command output, file path, or event that supports the timing entry.
